output.body:
# HMIS, HIS or HIMS, the software a hospital runs

## In plain words

The software a hospital runs day to day: registration, visits, orders,
results and billing. It goes by three names. HMIS is Hospital Management
Information System, HIS is Hospital Information System, and HIMS is
Hospital Information Management System. One system, three names, one
integration.

A facility uses it to publish records as the [HIP](hip.md) and to fetch
them as the [HIU](hiu.md), so the ABDM work is M2 and M3 rather than one
or the other. It must implement every [HI type](hi-type.md).

`HIS-` is also the prefix on every error code the [HPR](hpr.md) and the
[HFR](hfr.md) return. Those are [M4](m4.md) registry errors and have
nothing to do with hospital software.

## Before you start

Nothing. A glossary entry assumes no prior reading.

## What happens

Nothing happens here. This entry defines a term, it does not describe a call.

## How you know it worked

You have understood this when you can say which ABDM role a hospital plays
when it publishes a record, and which when it reads one.

## When it goes wrong

Implementing only the HI types you already produce. Every HI type is
mandatory for a hospital system.

reply.Text:
**HIMS** (Hospital Information Management System) is one of three names for the day-to-day software a hospital runs. The three interchangeable names are:

- **HMIS** — Hospital Management Information System
- **HIS** — Hospital Information System  
- **HIMS** — Hospital Information Management System

In the ABDM context, a HIMS is the software a health facility uses for registration, visits, orders, results, and billing. It plays **two different ABDM roles**:

1. **HIP (Health Information Provider)** — when publishing the facility's own records (M2)
2. **HIU (Health Information User)** — when fetching a patient's records from elsewhere (M3)

Because hospitals must act in both directions, HIMS implementations need to support all mandatory health information (HI) types.

**Note:** The prefix `HIS-` on error codes (like those returned by HPR and HFR registries) is unrelated to hospital software—those are M4 registry errors.

This definition is from the [ABDM HIE-CM glossary](https://abdm-docs.example.com/docs/hiecm/v3/getting-started/glossary#hmis).
